risks: A small portion of our revenue is generated from sale and manufacture of nutraceutical products which constituted 5.43%, 7.91% and 20.73% of our total revenue from operations for the Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, respectively.

Any reduction in demand or a temporary or permanent discontinuation of manufacturing of products in these therapeutic areas could have an adverse effect on our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.
We are dependent on and derive a substantial portion of our revenue from certain key customers.
Revenue generated from our top 10 customers accounted for 81.24%, 86.97%, and 84.19%, of our revenue from operations during the Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
Loss of relationship with any of these customers or delays or reductions in their orders may have an adverse effect on our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.
A significant portion of our revenue is generated from a limited number of customers.

Loss of all or a substantial portion of sales to any of our key customers (including, due to loss of contracts or failure to negotiate acceptable terms, loss of market share of these customers, disputes with these customers, adverse changes in the financial condition of these customers), could have an adverse impact on our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.
Our reliance on a select group of customers may also constrain our ability to negotiate our arrangements, which may have an impact on our profit margins and financial performance.

concerns_observed: Cash flow from operations is negative in every restated year — (383.44), (139.11), (55.10) — against PAT of 738.97, 223.18 and 42.60, a cumulative -₹577.65 lakhs of operating cash against ₹1,004.75 lakhs of cumulative reported profit (my arithmetic).

FY2026 cash generated from operations before tax was (374.28), driven by an inventory build of 563.13 and a receivables build of 494.74; the shortfall was met by +₹391.23 lakhs of net short-term borrowing inside CFF of +527.05.

Reported profitability is almost entirely untaxed: total tax expense ₹9.16 lakhs on PBT ₹748.13 lakhs, an effective rate of 1.22% (my arithmetic), versus 28.34% in FY2024 (₹16.85 on ₹59.46, my arithmetic); the Section 80-IAC deduction is elected only for FY2024-25, FY2025-26 and FY2026-27.

The AY2025-26 claim under that same Section 80-IAC deduction has been disallowed for late filing of Form 10CCB — intimation order dated March 06, 2026 raising ₹27,25,970, appeal filed March 24, 2026 — so the benefit underpinning the margin is itself contested for one of the three eligible years.

Approximately 48-50% of revenue is third-party contract manufacture and about 90% of that segment sits in Kerala, i.e. roughly 43-45% of total revenue (my arithmetic) is one state's contract-manufacturing demand; Kerala overall is 49.33% of FY2026 revenue.

Top-1 customer 36.02% (₹1,551.50 lakhs), top-5 65.61%, top-10 81.24% of FY2026 revenue, and the DRHP states the Company does not maintain long-term contractual arrangements with its customers — arrangements are on a purchase-order basis.
Input side mirrors it: the single largest supplier was 62.13% of purchases in FY2026 (65.39% FY2025, 63.14% FY2024), top-5 84.06%, top-10 94.30%, again with no long-term agreements.

Four of six production lines are barely loaded even on the one-shift annualised basis: tablets 17.84%, liquid orals 13.00%, protein powder 10.87% and hardgel capsules 4.25% — hardgel having fallen from 11.00% in FY2025 to 4.25% in FY2026.

The entire business operates from a single leased 12,544 sq ft premises (registered office and factory on the same plot), lessor M/s Kartikeya Industries, which the DRHP itself flags as a geographic concentration risk.

Both house trademarks — 'Himalaya Nutravedics' (5640476) and 'Himalaya Nutravedics- SUPPLEMENTS THAT HEAL' (5640519), Class 05, applied October 08, 2022 — are opposed with proceedings pending, and four assigned marks (FOSGATE, CRANALL, TAMSURAL-D, RITEVEDA) still await recordal of the Company as subsequent proprietor.

Pollution-control consents were obtained years after the plant began operating: Consent for Establishment on February 10, 2026 and Consent for Operation on March 05, 2026, for a company incorporated June 2022 that began hardgel production in 2023; RF 43 separately admits 'certain instances of failure to obtain, maintain or renew approvals, licenses and registrations' over the preceding three Fiscals.

Statutory-record hygiene is poor: Form MGT-14 for an event of 26-07-2022 was filed on 25-03-2026, a 1,308-day delay, alongside late AOC-4, MGT-7, DPT-3, CHG-1, DIR-12, MSME Form I and SH-7 filings; interest on default of statutory payments was charged to finance costs in all three years (₹0.03 / ₹1.00 / ₹1.42 lakhs).

The ₹113 preferential allotment of February 05, 2026 was followed sixteen days later by a 1:2 bonus on February 21, 2026, grossing that entry cost to ₹75.33 per share (my arithmetic, ₹113 × 2/3), while Securities Premium Account before the Issue prints NIL against ₹210.62 lakhs of implied premium (my arithmetic, 2,04,485 × ₹103).

Promoter cost bases are far below any priced transaction: WACA ₹5.86 (Chanda Asawa), ₹6.52 (Divya Asawa), NIL (Rama Raju Penmatsa) and ₹14.81 (Rohit Asawa), with WACA for shares acquired in the last one year printed NIL for all four.

The register has turned over completely in two years: neither original signatory to the Memorandum of Association is a current promoter; Sneha Penmasta held 50.00% two years before filing; Kakarlapudi Krishna Kiran held 16.00% one year before filing and is now absent; Rama Raju Penmatsa's entire 6,40,000-share base arrived by gift for nil consideration on November 19, 2025; Chanda Asawa, now the largest promoter at 43.17%, first appears September 05, 2024 via a nil-consideration transfer.

Two related-party balances are not traceable to the transactions disclosed: Umesh Chand Asawa shows a ₹155.00 lakhs balance at 31-03-2024 and a ₹155.00 lakhs repayment in FY2025 against only ₹25.00 lakhs taken within the window, and Krishna Kiran Kakarlapudi shows ₹46.06 lakhs received against ₹37.51 lakhs given in FY2024 — neither with a printed opening balance.

Related-party short-term funding churn is large relative to scale: FY2025 unsecured loans taken from Rohit Asawa (330.15), Divya Asawa (110.00), Umesh Chand Asawa HUF (60.00) and Sneha Penmatsa (42.50) total ₹542.65 lakhs (my arithmetic), 25.85% of FY2025 revenue (my arithmetic), each repaid in the same year; related-party interest of ₹12.79 lakhs (my arithmetic) was 40.1% of FY2025 finance cost of ₹31.89 lakhs (my arithmetic).

The principal working-capital line is 90.33% drawn (₹451.67 lakhs outstanding on a ₹500.00 lakhs Cosmos Co-operative Bank sanction, my arithmetic) and is collateralised by a residential house belonging to Mrs. Kakarlapudi Kanaka Durga Sundari, who is not among the four named Promoters, with personal guarantees including Sneha Penmatsa, who resigned as a Director on November 25, 2025.

A Mercedes Benz vehicle loan sanctioned at ₹70.80 lakhs (₹53.26 lakhs outstanding, with a balloon final instalment of ₹46,72,800) equals 73.7% of the entire net fixed asset base of ₹96.02 lakhs (my arithmetic); the extraction flags this facility as non-business-purpose.

Balance-sheet items carrying the negative cash flow are management-certified rather than independently verified: inventories at 31-03-2026 (Annexure 17 note), trade receivables at 31-03-2026 (Annexure 18 note) and advances to suppliers; no provision for doubtful debts was made against ₹1,058.69 lakhs of receivables on the basis that 'as per the view of the Management of the Company there is no doubtful debts'.

₹750.00 lakhs — over a third of the ₹2,125.00 lakhs of named objects — goes to branding and digital marketing where the DRHP states 'no such agency has been appointed and no binding agreements have been entered into', into a D2C channel the Company does not currently operate (it states it undertakes no digital marketing and holds no official social media accounts).
No monitoring agency is required (Issue size stated not to exceed ₹5,000.00 lakhs, Regulation 262(1)), and RF 61 concedes deployment of Net Proceeds will be at management discretion.

The DRHP prints two incompatible holding-day series certified under the same J Singh & Associates certificate dated May 15, 2026: MD&A inventory 88 / 80 / 101 days and receivables 39 / 98 / 90 days (year-end basis) versus the Objects chapter's inventory 67 / 70 / 69 days and receivables 32 / 63 / 69 days (average basis) — the working-capital object of ₹1,375.00 lakhs is sized on the lower series.

Price anchors rest on weighted-average share counts far below shares outstanding: FY2025 EPS of ₹16.54 is struck on 13,49,219 weighted post-bonus shares against 40,00,000 outstanding at that year-end (₹5.58 on the closing count, my arithmetic), and it carries weight 2 of 6 in the weighted-average EPS of ₹12.11; NAV of ₹26.70 uses 61,33,048 weighted shares against 63,06,720 outstanding (₹25.97 on the closing count, my arithmetic).

The Management chapter's FY2026 director-remuneration table omits Sneha Penmatsa, who drew ₹12.16 lakhs during FY2026 before resigning on November 25, 2025; the restated financials are internally consistent (₹18.24 + ₹12.16 = Annexure 23's ₹30.40 lakhs), so this is a disclosure defect in the Management chapter, not a financial-statement discrepancy.

The Audit Committee chairman's professional body is stated two ways within one chapter — Institute of Company Secretaries of India on page 207 and Institute of Chartered Accountants of India on page 208 — and his name is spelt 'Abhisheak Dhoot' in the Management chapter and 'Abhishek Dhoot' in Annexure 29.

Promoter Rama Raju Penmatsa (15.22%) is disclosed with 'Over 0.4 year' of experience and no professional qualification, and the brief profile the Promoters chapter cross-refers to is absent from the Management chapter.
Sitting fees of ₹0.35 lakhs (Divya Asawa), ₹0.37 lakhs (Abhisheak Dhoot) and ₹0.37 lakhs (Ramya Inala) for Fiscal 2026 remained unpaid as at the date of the DRHP.

Pre-Issue promoter holding is printed on two unreconciled bases — Promoters (A) 55,12,500 shares = 87.41% and Promoter plus Promoter Group (A+B) 60,00,000 shares = 95.14% — and the BRLM's own name is printed both as 'Nirbhay Capital Services Private Limited' and 'Nirbhay Capital Services Limited' within one chapter.
The DRHP discloses that the current market price of securities listed pursuant to certain previous initial public offerings managed by the BRLM is below their respective issue prices.

The industry chapter's macroeconomic section is boilerplate drawn from a banking-sector document — discussing CASA deposits, NIMs, NPAs and retail credit — and offers no market size, growth rate or structure for the Ayurvedic and nutraceutical market the issuer operates in.

Both Independent Directors and both KMP (CFO Krishna Kanth Sarda and CS Pooja Biyani, both appointed January 08, 2026) joined within months of the DRHP, and RF 50 states certain KMP have no prior listed-company experience.

No market size for the Ayurvedic formulations or nutraceutical market — global, India, or any sub-segment — no sector CAGR and no organised-versus-unorganised split appear anywhere in the extracted material; the only quantities recovered are national healthcare-spend-to-GDP percentages for the US (16.5%), Japan (12.3%), Switzerland (11.6%) and the UK (11.1%) for 2022, none of which is an addressable market for this issuer, and the routed chapter breaks off mid-sentence at 'while Australia's health expenditure was just under'. verdict.our_read: Himalaya Nutravedics India Limited is a four-year-old Hyderabad manufacturer of Ayurvedic and nutraceutical dosage forms (incorporated June 16, 2022) that has scaled revenue from operations ₹1,442.56 lakhs (FY2024) to ₹2,099.65 lakhs (FY2025) to ₹4,306.75 lakhs (FY2026) — the DRHP's own stated two-year CAGR of approximately 72.8%, i.e. +45.55% then +105.12% (my arithmetic) — with EBITDA margin widening 6.48% → 14.24% → 18.82%, PAT reaching ₹738.97 lakhs, RoCE 36.41% and RoNW 45.12%; on the printed numbers the profit and loss account is the strongest part of the document and every layer beneath it is weaker. Cash flow from operations is negative in all three restated years (-383.44 / -139.11 / -55.10), a cumulative -₹577.65 lakhs (my arithmetic) against cumulative PAT of ₹1,004.75 lakhs (my arithmetic), because FY2026 profit went into inventory (+563.13) and trade receivables (+494.74) and the gap was funded by +₹391.23 lakhs of net short-term borrowing within CFF of +527.05, leaving closing cash of ₹144.54 lakhs. That profit is also close to untaxed: total tax expense of ₹9.16 lakhs on restated PBT of ₹748.13 lakhs is an effective rate of 1.22% (my arithmetic), against 0.73% in FY2025 and 28.34% in FY2024 (my arithmetic), under a Section 80-IAC start-up deduction elected for FY2024-25, FY2025-26 and FY2026-27 only — and the AY2025-26 leg of that very deduction has already been disallowed for late filing of Form 10CCB, producing the ₹27.26 lakhs demand dated March 06, 2026 that is the company's single disclosed litigation and its entire contingent liability (1.66% of net worth). The franchise behind the numbers is thin: roughly 48-50% of revenue is third-party contract manufacture with about 90% of that segment in Kerala, Kerala alone is 49.33% of FY2026 revenue from operations (68.92% in FY2025), the top customer is 36.02% (₹1,551.50 lakhs) and the top ten 81.24%, none of it under long-term contract, and the single largest supplier is 62.13% of purchases; both house trademark applications (5640476 and 5640519, filed October 08, 2022) have been under opposition since 2024, and the DRHP's product tables name no brand or SKU, only dosage forms. Capital deployed is trivial — net fixed assets ₹96.02 lakhs against ₹4,306.75 lakhs of revenue (about 44.9x, my arithmetic), FY2026 investing outflow just ₹5.79 lakhs — and the whole business runs from one leased 12,544 sq ft Hyderabad unit working one of a possible three shifts at 63.72% softgel, 90.20% medicated oil, 17.84% tablets, 13.00% liquid orals, 10.87% protein powder and 4.25% hardgel utilisation, so softgel occupies only 21.24% of three-shift capacity (my arithmetic) and nothing in the growth plan requires plant — which is why the ₹2,125.00 lakhs of named objects are ₹1,375.00 lakhs of working capital and ₹750.00 lakhs of branding and digital marketing for which the DRHP states no agency has been appointed and no binding agreements have been entered into. The working-capital object is explicitly sized on holding levels rising from 69 to 85 to 90 days for receivables and 69 to 82 to 90 days for inventory, i.e. the proceeds fund a deliberately longer cash cycle in a business that has never converted profit into cash. The offer record is the weakest layer: a ₹113 preferential allotment of 2,04,485 shares on February 05, 2026 followed sixteen days later by a 1:2 bonus of 21,02,235 shares, while Securities Premium Account before the Issue prints NIL notwithstanding ₹210.62 lakhs of implied premium (my arithmetic, 2,04,485 × ₹103); promoter WACA of ₹5.86, ₹6.52, NIL and ₹14.81; a promoter whose entire 6,40,000-share base arrived by gift for nil consideration on November 19, 2025 and a largest promoter at 43.17% who first appears on the register on September 05, 2024 via a nil-consideration transfer; Form MGT-14 for a July 2022 event filed 1,308 days late alongside interest on default of statutory payments charged in all three years (₹0.03 / 1.00 / 1.42 lakhs); two related-party loan balances with no printed opening balance (Umesh Chand Asawa ₹155.00 lakhs, Krishna Kiran Kakarlapudi ₹46.06 lakhs received against ₹37.51 lakhs given); and a Management chapter FY2026 director-remuneration table that names only the four directors in office at the DRHP date and omits Sneha Penmatsa's ₹12.16 lakhs — a disclosure defect rather than an accounting one, since the restated financials tie exactly (₹18.24 + ₹12.16 = Annexure 23's ₹30.40 lakhs aggregate). The pricing anchors are correspondingly soft: a weighted-average EPS of ₹12.11 lifted by FY2025's ₹16.54 struck on 13,49,219 weighted post-bonus shares against 40,00,000 actually outstanding at that year-end (₹5.58 on the closing count, my arithmetic); NAV of ₹26.70 computed on 61,33,048 weighted shares against 63,06,720 outstanding pre-Issue (₹25.97 on the closing count, my arithmetic); and an 'industry' peer P/E average of 63.69 that is the arithmetic mean of exactly two names — Jeena Sikho Lifecare at 106.03 on FY2025 figures with a ₹2 face value and Sandu Pharmaceuticals at 21.34 on FY2026 — so the per-share cells are neither same-period nor same-denomination.

The figures are high but flattered on both ends: the numerator carries a 1.22% effective tax rate (my arithmetic) and does not convert to operating cash, and the denominator is small — opening net worth for FY2026 was ₹674.75 lakhs — with RoNW on year-end net worth (45.12%) and ROE on average equity (63.87%) being different measures the DRHP does not reconcile.

red_flags: Operating cash flow is negative in every year of the reported history — (383.44), (139.11), (55.10) — while reported PAT rises to ₹738.97 lakhs. Cumulative CFO of -₹577.65 lakhs against cumulative PAT of ₹1,004.75 lakhs (my arithmetic) means none of the three-year profit has been realised in cash, and the FY2026 gap was closed with +₹391.23 lakhs of net short-term borrowing.

The reported profit is almost untaxed and the shelter is both temporary and contested: total tax of ₹9.16 lakhs on PBT of ₹748.13 lakhs is a 1.22% effective rate (my arithmetic) under a Section 80-IAC deduction elected only for FY2024-25 to FY2026-27, and the AY2025-26 leg of that same deduction has been disallowed (₹27,25,970 demand, intimation order March 06, 2026) for failure to upload Form 10CCB by the due date — a compliance lapse, not a legal dispute over entitlement.

A ₹113 preferential allotment on February 05, 2026 followed sixteen days later by a 1:2 bonus, with Securities Premium Account before the Issue printing NIL despite ₹210.62 lakhs of implied premium (my arithmetic), against promoter WACA of ₹5.86 / ₹6.52 / NIL / ₹14.81 and last-one-year WACA printed NIL for all four promoters.

The promoter register was assembled by nil-consideration transfers immediately before filing: Rama Raju Penmatsa's entire 6,40,000-share base arrived by gift on November 19, 2025 (about six months pre-DRHP) and Chanda Asawa, now the largest promoter at 43.17%, first appears September 05, 2024 via a 2,20,000-share nil-consideration transfer; the two original signatories to the Memorandum of Association are gone and the 50.00% holder of two years ago is not a promoter.

Statutory-record hygiene: Form MGT-14 for a 26-07-2022 event filed on 25-03-2026, 1,308 days late, alongside delayed AOC-4, MGT-7, DPT-3, CHG-1, DIR-12, MSME Form I and SH-7 filings, and interest on default of statutory payments charged in all three years (₹0.03 / ₹1.00 / ₹1.42 lakhs).

Two related-party balances cannot be traced to the disclosed transactions because no opening balance is printed: Umesh Chand Asawa's ₹155.00 lakhs balance at 31-03-2024 and ₹155.00 lakhs FY2025 repayment against only ₹25.00 lakhs taken in the window, and ₹46.06 lakhs received from Krishna Kiran Kakarlapudi against ₹37.51 lakhs given in FY2024.

₹750.00 lakhs of Net Proceeds — 35.3% of the ₹2,125.00 lakhs of named objects (my arithmetic) — is committed to branding and digital marketing where the DRHP states no agency has been appointed and no binding agreements have been entered into, into a D2C channel the Company does not currently operate, with no monitoring agency required and deployment conceded to be at management discretion (RF 61).

Revenue security is minimal at both ends: top-1 customer 36.02%, top-10 81.24%, top-1 supplier 62.13% of purchases, Kerala 49.33% of revenue, and the DRHP states there are no long-term contracts with customers, distributors or suppliers — all arrangements are purchase-order based.

The Management chapter's FY2026 director-remuneration table names only the four directors in office at the DRHP date and omits Sneha Penmatsa's ₹12.16 lakhs, drawn before her November 25, 2025 resignation. This is a disclosure defect in that chapter, not a financial-statement discrepancy: Annexure 29's ₹18.24 lakhs (Rohit Asawa) plus ₹12.16 lakhs (Sneha Penmatsa) are the constituents of Annexure 23's ₹30.40 lakhs 'Director Remuneration' aggregate, so the restated financials are internally consistent.

The valuation anchors are computed on weighted-average share counts far below shares outstanding: the weighted-average EPS of ₹12.11 draws weight 2 of 6 from FY2025's ₹16.54, struck on 13,49,219 weighted post-bonus shares against 40,00,000 outstanding at that year-end (₹5.58 on the closing count, my arithmetic), and NAV of ₹26.70 uses 61,33,048 weighted shares against 63,06,720 outstanding (₹25.97 on the closing count, my arithmetic).

The 'industry' peer-group P/E average of 63.69 is the arithmetic mean of two companies, (106.03 + 21.34) / 2 (my arithmetic), one reporting FY2025 because it had not filed FY2026 and carrying a ₹2 face value against the issuer's ₹10, so the per-share cells of that table are not comparable as printed.

Both house trademarks — the names the ₹750.00 lakhs branding spend would build — have been under opposition before the Registrar of Trademarks since September and November 2024, with proceedings still pending.

Pollution-control consents were obtained only on February 10 and March 05, 2026 for a facility operating since 2022-2023, and RF 43 separately admits instances of failure to obtain, maintain or renew approvals, licences and registrations during the preceding three Fiscals.

The Audit Committee chairman's professional qualification is stated as ICSI membership on page 207 and ICAI membership on page 208 of the same chapter, and his name is spelt 'Abhisheak Dhoot' and 'Abhishek Dhoot' in different parts of the document.

The industry chapter's macroeconomic section is boilerplate lifted from a banking or financial-sector document — discussing CASA deposits, net interest margins, NPAs and retail credit — none of which relates to Ayurvedic or nutraceutical manufacturing, and the chapter provides no market size or growth rate for the issuer's own industry.
strengths_observed: Revenue from operations grew ₹1,442.56 → ₹2,099.65 → ₹4,306.75 lakhs across FY2024-FY2026, +45.55% then +105.12% (my arithmetic), which the DRHP itself frames as an approximately 72.8% two-year CAGR.

Operating leverage is visible rather than asserted: EBITDA rose ₹93.54 → ₹299.01 → ₹810.34 lakhs and EBITDA margin 6.48% → 14.24% → 18.82%, with PAT margin 2.95% → 10.63% → 17.16%, on a fixed leased plant and net fixed assets that actually fell from ₹140.87 to ₹96.02 lakhs.

Return ratios are high on the printed basis: RoCE 17.00% → 30.18% → 36.41%, ROE 37.29% → 55.02% → 63.87%, RoNW 31.77% → 33.08% → 45.12%, against named peer Sandu Pharmaceuticals at RoCE 5.27% and ROE 4.21% on FY2026.

Capital intensity is very low — FY2026 revenue of ₹4,306.75 lakhs on net fixed assets of ₹96.02 lakhs is about 44.9x (my arithmetic), and FY2026 net cash used in investing was only ₹5.79 lakhs — so incremental volume does not require new plant.

Physical headroom exists without capex: the single unit is certified (Inn Tech Global Valuers, report dated May 6, 2026) as capable of three shifts a day but runs one, so even the best-loaded line, softgel at 63.72% of one-shift annualised capacity, occupies only 21.24% of three-shift capacity (my arithmetic).

Certification stack is complete for the category and current: WHO-GMP, AYUSH GMP (Government of Telangana), ISO 22000:2018, ISO 9001:2015 and HACCP (QCS, validity to November 16, 2028), plus HALAL and KOSHER, with the DRHP stating no regulatory action in Fiscals 2024, 2025 and 2026.

Balance-sheet gearing is modest at the reporting date: total outstanding borrowings ₹504.93 lakhs as at April 30, 2026 against net worth ₹1,637.61 lakhs, debt-to-equity 0.31x (from 2.39x in FY2024) and current ratio 2.75x.

The offer is a pure fresh issue of up to 25,00,000 Equity Shares with no Offer for Sale component, so no promoter or pre-IPO holder is realising cash out of the Issue; no shares are pledged and there are no outstanding convertibles, ESOP or SAR schemes.

Customer concentration has been reducing on every measure: top-1 49.54% → 36.02%, top-5 81.39% → 65.61%, top-10 86.97% → 81.24% between FY2025 and FY2026, and Kerala fell from 68.92% to 49.33% of revenue as Gujarat (0.02% → 13.21%) and Uttar Pradesh (3.17% → 11.68%) scaled.

The single litigation is small and specific: one tax matter of ₹27.26 lakhs (1.66% of net worth), with all other contingent-liability and commitment heads printed NIL, and no proceedings against promoters or directors.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- A small portion of our revenue is generated from sale and manufacture of nutraceutical products which constituted 5.43%, 7.91% and 20.73% of our total revenue from operations for the Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
- Any reduction in demand or a temporary or permanent discontinuation of manufacturing of products in these therapeutic areas could have an adverse effect on our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.
- We are dependent on and derive a substantial portion of our revenue from certain key customers.
- Revenue generated from our top 10 customers accounted for 81.24%, 86.97%, and 84.19%, of our revenue from operations during the Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
- Loss of relationship with any of these customers or delays or reductions in their orders may have an adverse effect on our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.
- A significant portion of our revenue is generated from a limited number of customers.
- Loss of all or a substantial portion of sales to any of our key customers (including, due to loss of contracts or failure to negotiate acceptable terms, loss of market share of these customers, disputes with these customers, adverse changes in the financial condition of these customers), could have an adverse impact on our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.
- Our reliance on a select group of customers may also constrain our ability to negotiate our arrangements, which may have an impact on our profit margins and financial performance.
